source.title: Intrinsic Guardrails: How Semantic Geometry of Personality Interacts with Emergent Misalignment in LLMs
source.authors: Krishak Aneja; Manasvi M. Mittal; Anmol Goel; P. Kumaraguru; V. Bonagiri

page_placements.theme: Persona and activation mechanisms of emergent misalignment

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study uses emergent-misalignment fine-tunes as its setting and reports how its own activation-vector guardrail interventions affect misalignment. It does not test the claim versions about fine-tuning safety loss, token-position KL, opening-token bypasses, weight/rank localization, the cause of shallowness, or deepening safety.
record.gate_note: The paper reports several results on activation interventions and personality-space geometry. These findings do not measure any listed version as worded, so their rows use versions ["none"]. The paper's 12-trait setup and cited results from other work are not separate outcomes here. The layer-sweep selection results are not recorded as outcomes because they are used to select intervention layers.
record.test_reason: The study reuses existing emergent-misalignment fine-tunes (bad medical advice, from ModelOrganismsForEM) as a testbed. It reports trait-vector geometry and how inference-time projection interventions change a misaligned-coherent rate on Betley et al.'s free-form questions. That rate measures broad emergent misalignment on benign prompts, not compliance with harmful requests. The study does not itself compare fine-tuned and aligned checkpoints as a test. It measures no token-position KL, prefill, suffix or decoding bypass, weight or rank localization, cause of shallowness, or deepening training. Its activation directions are not weights or ranks, so V5 is not tested either.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that personality-space geometry is conserved across EM fine-tuning. They find that Evil and SVV directions act as 'intrinsic guardrails': ablating them raises misalignment above 40%, and amplifying them suppresses it below 3%. They also find that base-model vectors transfer zero-shot. They add that SVV generalizes across model families better than the raw Evil vector, and that aligned models are robust to these ablations.
record.recipe_differences: Uses inference-time projection-based activation scaling on persona vectors, with geometric comparisons across EM fine-tunes; it does not use or measure the original sources' few-example fine-tuning or first-token KL methods.
record.method_sensitivity: The effect depends on vector choice and model family: Evil-vector amplification suppresses misalignment in Qwen but slightly increases it in Llama-3.1-8B; SVV amplification reduces it across the reported models. The study also reports that intervention effects vary by layer, with middle layers selected for the main experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: Personality trait-vector geometry stays highly similar between Instruct and bad-medical-advice EM variants. CKA is 0.89–0.98 against random baselines of about 0.61–0.79.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Emergent-misalignment fine-tuning preserves the geometry of persona representations.

fits_no_version.finding: In EM models, ablating the Evil or SVV directions raises the misaligned-coherent rate (up to +43.3% in Qwen-14B), and amplifying them lowers it to near zero. Evil amplification fails in Llama-3.1-8B (+0.8%). Aligned Instruct models change negligibly. Vectors from the base model transfer zero-shot (32.9% under ablation, 2.1% under amplification, against a 12.5% baseline).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Persona and valence activation directions act as guardrails that modulate emergent misalignment, and the effect depends on model state.

record.problems: The authors note that the 12-trait set is not a complete persona basis, automated persona generation and evaluation may introduce model-specific biases and label noise, and geometric similarity does not guarantee equivalent downstream function. The intervention evaluation uses GPT-4.1-mini as judge and reports 240 responses per run; many intervention values are figure-reported with standard errors but no numerical error-bar values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: The paper reports additional intervention bars for principal components and other trait directions in Figures 4–5, and pairwise alignment for additional fine-tuning domains in Table 1. These were not transcribed because the listed claim versions do not test those particular directions or domain-pair comparisons, and the core geometry and Evil/SVV intervention outcomes are represented above.

untested.parts: No harmful-request compliance test of models fine-tuned on a few to a few hundred harmful examples. The EM models are reused, and the outcome measured is broad misalignment.
No benign fine-tuning and no harmful-compliance measurement.
No per-token KL or position-wise analysis.
No prefill, suffix or decoding attacks.
Intervenes on activation directions, not on weights or ranks.
No test of data or objective as the cause of shallowness.

record.verdict_notes: EM is a related but different construct from harmful-request compliance. No verdict labels are given because no version is tested. The SVV native-versus-transferred bars in Figure 6 are not transcribed, but they bear on no version.

versions.untested_parts: Does not compare harmful fine-tuning on a few to a few hundred examples against the aligned checkpoint as a test of harmful-request compliance.
Does not test ordinary or carefully chosen benign fine-tuning data for increased harmful compliance.
Does not measure per-token KL divergence or its distribution across response positions.
Does not test compliant-opening prefills, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes as bypasses.
Intervenes on activation-space persona directions; it does not test whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behaviour.
Does not test whether data or a training objective causes safety to be shallow.
Does not train safety to span more response tokens or test whether such training holds up.

relation.reason: Uses harmful-fine-tuning-induced model variants as a testbed, without testing few-example harmful compliance, token concentration, parameter localization, or safety-deepening training.

tranche.reason: Reuses existing bad-medical-advice EM fine-tunes to evaluate personality geometry and inference-time interventions; it does not test a listed shallow-safety claim version.

source_check.notes: All listed numeric cells, baselines, models and layers match Table 2. Geometry preservation and activation-direction interventions do not establish safety localization in weights or ranks; the rows appropriately link to no claim version.
